transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um... well, what finally pushed me to come in is that I'm just really struggling at work lately. I manage a health clinic, so I do a lot of data tracking, and I can start pulling an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in one of our clinic metrics meetings with every intention of paying attention. Actually, we just had a huge meeting on Tuesday because the new compliance guidelines came down from corporate, and they want everything color-coded on the new dashboards now, which honestly feels a bit redundant since the old system worked perfectly fine for the last five years. My husband said I shouldn't let corporate policy changes get to me so much, but it's hard when you're the one training the staff, you know? 

Wait, what was I... oh, right. The meetings. Anyway, I'll be sitting there, trying to track the metrics, and within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far off that I’m just rereading the exact same numbers on the screen over and over again. Or someone will ask me a question and I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion.
Have you always had trouble paying attention in meetings or is this a relatively recent problem for you?

Well, it hasn't always been this bad. It really became a noticeable issue after my promotion, which was about two years and four months ago. I remember the exact timing because it was right around the same time we decided to redo our kitchen, and living through a renovation while taking on a new role was... well, let's just say we ate a lot of takeout. We found this amazing little Thai place down the street, though. Their Pad Kee Mao is just incredible. My husband can't handle the spice at all, he always asks them to make it mild, but I absolutely love it. 

Anyway, where was I? Oh, the promotion. Right. So, with the new title, I suddenly had this much larger portfolio to manage. Before that, I had all these little systems I relied on to keep myself on track, you know? Like my specific daily planner and my inbox rules. I used to buy this one specific brand of notebook from Staples because the paper was thick enough that my pens wouldn't bleed through to the other side. I hate when you write on Tuesday and it ruins Wednesday's page. But they actually stopped making the layout I like, which is so frustrating. 

But yeah, the new workload and the larger portfolio just completely overwhelmed the systems I used to rely on. There were just too many moving parts all of a sudden, and... wait, I'm sorry, what exactly did you ask me? I kind of lost my train of thought there.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless, especially in situations where you need to sit still?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm a particularly fidgety person. I don't bounce my leg or anything like that. My brother does that, actually. Whenever we go out to dinner, he's constantly shaking the whole table, and it drives me absolutely crazy. We went to this Italian place for my mom's birthday last month—beautiful restaurant, they have this amazing handmade pasta—and he was just bouncing his leg the entire time. I finally had to ask him to stop because I was trying to drink my wine and the glass was practically vibrating. They had this really nice Chianti, too, which is usually hard to find by the glass. 

But no, I don't do that. I usually just sit there. Even when my mind is wandering off to a million different places, my body is pretty still. I guess I might play with my pen sometimes during those metrics meetings, but that's just because I like the clicky ones. Honestly, I'm more likely to just zone out completely than to start squirming around.
Do you find yourself making careless mistakes in your work, such as forgetting important details or making errors in your reports?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I make careless mistakes like that. I'm actually pretty thorough when I'm pulling those EPIC reports. I always double-check the dates because last year, someone—not me, it was one of the new coordinators—pulled a whole quarter's worth of data using the wrong fiscal calendar. We had to redo the entire presentation for the board, and the board members are already so picky about how the graphs look. There's this one guy on the board, Dr. Henderson, he always insists on having pie charts instead of bar graphs. I don't know why, bar graphs are so much easier to read when you're comparing clinic volumes, but he just loves his pie charts. He's retiring next year, though, so maybe we can finally switch back. 

But yeah, I don't really make errors like that. I might take twice as long to finish the report because I keep losing my place, but the numbers themselves are usually right. What did you ask me about forgetting? Oh, important details. No, I don't think I forget the important stuff. I just... take a really long time to get it done.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I'm not really an interrupter. Honestly, I'm usually the one who has to sit and listen to everyone else talk. Working in clinic management, you get a lot of people venting to you, and you just have to let them get it out. 

Like our lead scheduling coordinator, Sarah. She is lovely, she really is, but she will talk your ear off about her cats if you let her. She just adopted this new rescue, a Siamese mix, I think? It has those bright blue eyes. I've always wanted a cat, but my husband is terribly allergic. We had to get a poodle mix because they have hair instead of fur, so it doesn't trigger his allergies as badly. He still sneezes constantly during the spring, though, especially when the oak pollen gets really bad. We had to buy one of those expensive HEPA air purifiers for the bedroom just so he could sleep through the night. It hums a little bit, which took me a while to get used to, but now I actually kind of like the white noise... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what was the question? Did you ask about my staff? Oh, blurting things out! Right, sorry. No, no, I don't do that. I mostly just stay quiet and wait for them to finish talking.
Do you have trouble keeping your workspace or desk organized?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my desk at work is actually pretty tidy. I'm really particular about where I keep my things. I have this little organizer for my pens—I told you I like the clicky ones, right? Well, I have them all sorted by color because I use different colors for different types of notes. Blue is for staffing issues, red is for budget, and black is just for general to-do lists. 

I actually got the organizer at this little boutique stationary shop downtown. It's one of those places that sells really expensive paper that you're almost afraid to write on. I went in there looking for a birthday card for my sister-in-law. She's impossible to shop for. Last year I got her a gift card to her favorite spa, and she complained that it didn't cover the tip. Can you believe that? So this year I just decided to get her a really nice card and call it a day. The shop had these beautiful letterpress cards, though. They're made on these antique printing presses, and you can actually feel the indentation of the letters on the paper. It's fascinating how they do it. I watched a documentary about it once on PBS...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, my desk. Right. No, I don't really have trouble keeping it organized. I like having a clean space. It's just getting the actual work done while sitting at the clean desk that's the hard part.
Do you often avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort?

Well, um... yeah, actually. I do tend to put off the really dense stuff. Like, if I have to do a big policy review or block out time for long data analysis, I'll push it to the very end of the day. The thought of just sitting there with all that detailed reading and having to think that hard... it almost feels physically hard to start, you know? 

Like last week, we had this massive update to the telehealth compliance guidelines. It was, I don't know, maybe forty pages of just pure legal jargon. I kept finding other things to do. I watered the plants in the waiting room, which isn't even my job, but the poor pothos was looking so droopy. I think the AC vent blows right on it. Plants really don't like drafts, especially tropical ones. My grandmother had this incredible sunroom filled with orchids, and she was militant about the temperature in there. She had this little vintage thermometer on the wall with a brass dial. It was beautiful. I wonder what happened to that thermometer when they sold the house... my cousin probably took it. She always had an eye for antiques. She runs this little vintage shop out in Oregon now. Sells mostly mid-century furniture. I love that style, but the original pieces are just so expensive now. 

Anyway... what was the question? Oh, avoiding things. Right. Yeah, those long, heavy tasks... I just keep finding other things to do until I absolutely have to sit down and force myself to read them.
Have you noticed any negative impact on your personal relationships or daily life outside of work due to your difficulty with focus and task completion?

Yeah, I mean... it definitely spills over. It's not just the desk stuff. At work, my delays have started affecting clinic reporting deadlines, which is really embarrassing. The other teams end up waiting on me to finish my part. And outside of work, I've actually had to step back from leading parts of these volunteer health workshops I used to do. I just couldn't reliably keep all the planning pieces moving. 

It was really disappointing because I loved doing those workshops. We held them at this community center downtown, the one with the big brick courtyard? They have this amazing community garden out back. The tomatoes they grow are huge, like the size of softballs. I tried growing tomatoes on my patio last summer, but the squirrels kept getting to them before they were ripe. They are so bold! One of them actually sat on the railing and stared right at me while eating a green tomato. My husband thought it was hilarious, but I was so mad. I even bought this spicy pepper spray that's supposed to deter them, but I think it just seasoned the tomatoes for them. I ended up giving up and just buying them from the farmers market. There's this one vendor who sells these beautiful heirloom varieties... the purple Cherokees are my absolute favorite for sandwiches. A little mayo, salt, pepper on toasted sourdough... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my focus affecting things. Right, sorry. Yes, the reporting deadlines at the clinic and having to quit my volunteer planning. It's just getting too hard to juggle it all.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you're unable to focus or complete tasks?

Um, anxious? I don't... I don't think so. Not really anxious. I mean, it's frustrating, sure, but I wouldn't say I get overwhelmed or panicky about it. I just sort of... accept that it's going to take me longer. 

Like, when I was trying to finish that volunteer scheduling before I quit, I'd just sit there staring at the spreadsheet. Spreadsheets are so tedious anyway. I tried color-coding the cells to make it more interesting. I used this really nice pastel palette I found online. It was supposed to be inspired by sea glass. Have you ever gone hunting for sea glass? We went to the coast a few years ago, up near Mendocino, and the beaches there are just covered in it. You have to go early in the morning, right after high tide, to find the really good pieces. I found this one piece of cobalt blue glass that was perfectly frosted and smooth. It was gorgeous. I brought it home and put it in this little decorative bowl on my coffee table. The bowl is hand-thrown pottery. I took a ceramics class once at the community college. It is so much harder than it looks on TV. The clay just collapses if you don't pull it up right. I ended up making a lot of very lopsided ashtrays, which is funny because nobody in my house even smokes...

Wait, sorry. What was the question? Anxious? Oh, right. No, I don't really get anxious or overwhelmed about not finishing things. It's just more annoying than anything else.
Do you often feel restless or have an inability to engage in activities quietly in your free time?

Restless? No, I don't really feel restless. I mean, I can definitely sit still and do things quietly. I read a lot in my free time. I've been trying to get through this huge biography of Florence Nightingale. It's fascinating, really. Did you know she actually carried a pet owl around in her pocket? She rescued it from some kids in Athens. I can't imagine trying to keep a bird in your pocket. My neighbor has a parrot, an African Grey, I think. It is so loud. In the summer when we both have our windows open, I can hear it whistling the theme song to The Andy Griffith Show. It's funny the first two times, but after an hour, it really gets on your nerves. I tried talking to her about it, but she just says he's "expressing himself." She's one of those people who treats her pets like actual human children. She even knits little sweaters for her dachshunds in the winter. They do look pretty cute, I have to admit. I knit a scarf once, just a simple garter stitch, but the edges were all wonky. I think my tension was too tight. My grandmother was an amazing knitter...

Sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, being restless. Right. No, I don't really have that problem. I'm perfectly fine just sitting quietly with a book or watching TV.
Do you feel like your difficulties with focus and task completion are significantly affecting your overall well-being or happiness?

Well... I don't know about my overall happiness. I guess it's frustrating, but I wouldn't say I'm deeply unhappy because of it. It's more just this constant low-level annoyance with myself. 

Like, I try to keep things positive, you know? I actually started keeping a gratitude journal a few months ago to help with my well-being. It's this beautiful leather-bound book I found at a craft fair. The artisan who made it uses this traditional bookbinding technique... coptic stitching, I think it's called? You can see the thread along the spine. It lays completely flat when you open it, which is so nice for writing. I bought a special fountain pen to use with it, too. It has a medium nib and I got this ink called 'Midnight Blue.' It takes a little longer to dry, though. I accidentally smudged a whole page last week because I closed the book too fast. It smeared right across this entry I wrote about my niece's graduation. She just finished her nursing degree, which I'm so proud of. The ceremony was outdoors, and it was so hot that day. We were all fanning ourselves with the programs. They had this jazz band playing while people were finding their seats, and the saxophone player was incredible. I used to play the clarinet in middle school, but I could never get the reed to sound right. It always squeaked...

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, if this is affecting my well-being. Right. Um, no, I wouldn't say it's ruining my happiness or anything. I'm generally doing okay, just... annoyed that I can't seem to stay on track.
Do you think your mind wandering and difficulty staying focused are the main reasons you're having trouble completing tasks, or is it something else entirely?

Well, yeah, I think the mind wandering is definitely the main thing. It's actually what finally pushed me to come in and see you. I'll sit down at my desk to run an EPIC quality report, or I'll be in a clinic metrics meeting with the department heads, and I have every intention of paying attention and tracking the data. But within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far off that I'm rereading the same row of numbers over and over, or I suddenly realize I missed the entire point of the discussion. 

It happened just last Tuesday in the monthly review. The Chief of Surgery was talking, and he has this very deep, booming voice. It reminded me of this voice actor who does the audiobooks I listen to. I've been listening to a lot of historical fiction lately. The narrator for this one series about the Tudor court is just phenomenal. He does all the different accents—the French ambassadors, the Scottish lords. It's so immersive. I actually started looking up flights to London on my phone under the table because I got this sudden urge to go see Hampton Court Palace. My sister went a few years ago and she said the gardens are just spectacular. They have this huge maze that was planted in the 1600s. I love a good maze. We took my niece to a corn maze last Halloween, the one out by the old highway. It took us over an hour to find our way out, and it was so muddy. I ruined a perfectly good pair of suede boots. I tried cleaning them with that special brush, but the mud was just caked in...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, the mind wandering. Yes, that's exactly it. I just can't seem to stay focused on the task or the meeting, and then I'm completely lost.

Do you think your difficulty with focus and staying on task is the main problem you're experiencing, or are there other issues, like memory problems or difficulty with motivation, that might be contributing to your struggles?

Well, I don't think it's my memory, really. I remember things fine once I actually pay attention to them. And motivation... I don't know, maybe? But it's more like... I find myself putting off the really dense stuff. Like, as a manager, I have to do these huge policy reviews and long blocks of data analysis, and I just keep pushing them until late in the day. Because the thought of sitting there, with that much detailed reading and thinking... it feels almost physically hard to start. 

It's like when I try to start a new workout routine. I bought this stationary bike during the pandemic, one of those fancy ones with the screen where the instructors yell at you. The delivery guys had such a hard time getting it up my stairs. My staircase is really narrow, it's an older house, built in the twenties. It still has the original hardwood floors, which are beautiful, but they creak so loudly. My cat, Barnaby, hates the creaking. He's a rescue, part Maine Coon, so he's massive. He actually sleeps on the seat of the stationary bike now. It's basically a very expensive cat bed. I tried buying him one of those heated beds, but he prefers the bike. Cats are so funny like that. My sister's cat will only sleep in Amazon boxes. She ordered a new blender last week—one of those high-speed ones that can make hot soup—and the cat claimed the box before she even unpacked the blender. I've always wanted one of those blenders. I love making butternut squash soup in the fall. I add a little bit of nutmeg and some toasted pumpkin seeds on top... 

Oh, gosh. I'm sorry. I completely lost the thread again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the focus thing and avoiding tasks. Yeah, I just... I put off those heavy mental tasks because it's just so daunting to even begin them.
Do you think your difficulty with focus is the primary issue you're dealing with, or is there something else that you feel is more problematic?

Well, I mean, I think it's mainly the focus. I don't really know what else it would be. I guess I haven't really thought about if there's something else that's worse. It just feels like everything comes back to the fact that I can't keep my brain on a straight track. 

It's like trying to herd cats, which, speaking of Barnaby... he got out yesterday. I was bringing in the groceries, and I had this huge bag of potting soil because I decided I'm going to repot all my indoor plants this weekend. I have this beautiful Monstera that's just outgrowing its pot. The roots are actually coming out the bottom. I bought this ceramic planter at a local pottery studio, the one downtown near the old theater. They do these glazing classes on Thursday nights. I went with my friend Sarah a few months ago, and we made these little tapas plates. Mine came out a bit lopsided, but I use it to hold my keys by the front door. Anyway, I was propping the door open with the potting soil, and Barnaby just shot right past me. He made it all the way to Mrs. Higgins' yard next door before he got scared of her sprinkler system. She has one of those motion-sensor ones to keep the deer away from her hostas. Deer will eat absolutely anything, won't they? They completely decimated my sister's tulip bulbs last spring...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um... I'm not really sure if there's anything else that's more problematic. I think it's just the focus thing. That's the main hurdle, really.
Do you think your difficulty with focus and staying on task is something that you've always experienced to some degree, or is it a relatively new development in your life?

Well, honestly, it's always been there. It's not new at all. Even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. And my mother... oh, she always had to sit with me at the kitchen table just to make sure I finished my homework. I was always losing track of assignments or leaving my books at school. 

Our kitchen table was this big, round oak thing. My parents bought it at an antique auction right after they got married. It had this huge scratch down the middle from when my brother tried to fix his roller skates on it. He loved those skates. They were the old-fashioned kind with four wheels, the ones you had to strap over your shoes. We used to go to the roller rink every Friday night. They played all this great disco music, and they had a snack bar that sold those giant soft pretzels with the cheese dip. I can still smell the melted cheese and the floor wax. They don't make pretzels like that anymore, do they? Now everything is frozen and microwaved. I bought some frozen pretzels at the grocery store last week for my niece when she came over, and they just tasted like cardboard. She didn't mind, though. She was too busy playing this game on her tablet where you build a city out of blocks. I tried playing it with her, but I kept putting the buildings in the wrong places...

Oh, dear. I'm sorry. I drifted off again. But yes, to answer your question, this has been an issue for as long as I can remember. It's definitely not a new thing.
Do you think your difficulty with focus and staying on task is related to your level of interest in the task, or does it happen regardless of how interesting you find the task?

Well, that's the thing. I used to think it was just because I was bored. But what finally pushed me to come in and see you is that it's happening with things I *want* to do, or things I know are really important. Like, I can sit down to review an EPIC quality report, or I'll be in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking the whole thing. I'm a health services manager, so this is my bread and butter. I actually like looking at the data, usually. 

But then, within a few minutes, my mind has just drifted so far away. I'll catch myself rereading the same row of numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the point of the discussion the doctors were just having. It's so embarrassing. Speaking of the clinic meetings, they always cater them with these awful dry turkey wraps. I don't know who picked the catering company, probably someone in corporate, but they always put way too much mayonnaise on them, and the lettuce is always wilted. It's a shame, because there's this fantastic little deli just two blocks from the hospital. They do this incredible pastrami on rye. My dad used to take me to a deli just like it when I was a kid. He always ordered the pastrami, and he'd get me a black and white cookie. Have you ever had a real, authentic black and white cookie? The frosting has to be slightly hard on the outside but soft underneath, and the cake part should be almost like a shortbread... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Interest level. Yeah, so even when it's something I need to do or want to do, like those metrics meetings, I just can't seem to stay with it. My mind just goes for a walk without me.
Do you find it harder to focus in certain situations or environments, or is it equally difficult across all parts of your life?

Well, it's pretty much everywhere, but the consequences are definitely worse at work. Like, my delays have actually started affecting the clinic reporting deadlines. It's awful because it makes the other teams have to wait on me to finish my part before they can do theirs. I hate feeling like I'm holding everyone up. We use this shared dashboard system, and you can literally see whose tasks are pending, so there's this little red flag next to my name for everyone to see. It reminds me of when I was in a bowling league a few years ago. They had these big overhead screens that showed everyone's scores and whose turn it was. I was on a team with three other women from the neighborhood. We called ourselves the Pin Pals, which is so cheesy, I know, but we thought it was hilarious at the time. We actually got matching bowling shirts made. They were this bright turquoise color with our names embroidered on the front in pink thread. I still have mine in the back of my closet somewhere. I should probably donate it, but I have a hard time getting rid of clothes. I have this one sweater I bought in college that has a hole in the elbow, but I just can't part with it because it's so soft. It's cashmere, you know? Real cashmere is so expensive now. 

Anyway... um, where was I? Oh, right, the delays. Yeah, so the work stuff is bad, but it's also happening outside of work. I've actually had to step back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops I do in the community. I just can't reliably keep all the planning pieces moving anymore. I'd forget to confirm the venue or miss the deadline to order the printed materials, and it was just getting to be too much. So I guess it really is affecting everything, no matter where I am.
Do you think your difficulties with focus and staying on task are more related to problems with attention or to being easily distracted by your surroundings?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I've never really thought about the difference between the two. I guess it could be both? Like, sometimes I'll be trying to read a policy update, and I'll just look up and notice something out the window. 

My office at the clinic looks out over the visitor parking garage, but there's this one big maple tree right on the corner. The other day, there was this squirrel trying to carry an entire bagel up the trunk. A whole bagel! It must have gotten it from the dumpster behind the cafeteria. The cafeteria actually just switched food vendors last month, which was a huge ordeal with the budget committee. They used to have this terrible salad bar where the cucumbers were always slimy, but now they have a hot food station. I had their meatloaf on Tuesday, and it wasn't half bad. It reminded me of the meatloaf my grandmother used to make. She always put a hard-boiled egg right in the middle of it. Have you ever seen that? When you slice it, there's a perfect circle of egg in every piece. She used to serve it with these mashed potatoes that had way too much butter in them, but they were so good. She had this beautiful vintage potato ricer that made them perfectly smooth... 

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely lost the thread. I'm sorry. You were asking about distractions versus attention. Honestly, I really don't know if it's my surroundings pulling me away or just my own brain wandering off on its own. I haven't really noticed a pattern, just that my mind won't stay where I need it to.
Do you think your difficulty with focus is something that you experience across all situations, or are there specific times or activities where you feel more focused and able to concentrate?

I'm really not sure. I haven't noticed any specific times where I feel more focused, honestly. I've actually tried to find things that might hold my attention better, just to see. Like, a few months ago I decided to take up knitting, thinking maybe keeping my hands busy would help me zone in. 

I went down to this lovely little yarn shop on Main Street, the one right next to the old art deco movie theater. The owner there, her name is Barbara, she was incredibly helpful. She has this beautiful golden retriever that just sleeps in the corner of the shop all day. He is the sweetest thing, his name is Barnaby. I used to have a golden retriever when I was in my twenties. They really are just the absolute best dogs, so gentle and loyal. Mine used to love swimming in the lake behind our first house. We had this old wooden dock out back that was always giving everyone splinters. My husband at the time tried to sand it down one summer, but the wood was just too rotted. We eventually had to replace the whole thing with that composite decking material, which is so much more expensive up front, but honestly it's worth it because you never have to stain it. Staining a deck is such backbreaking work, especially in the humidity we get around here in July... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, if I can concentrate better on certain things. No, I don't think so. Because even with the knitting, I just end up dropping stitches or losing count of my rows because my mind wanders off to something else entirely. So yeah, I can't really think of any situation where the focus comes easily.
Do you feel like your difficulty with focus is worse when you're stressed or upset about something?

I mean, I don't really know if stress makes it worse. I haven't really paid attention to that. I guess I'm always a little stressed? Working at the clinic is just constant pressure. Especially with the new electronic health record system they rolled out last quarter. It was supposed to streamline everything, but the interface is just so clunky. 

The training they gave us for it was completely inadequate, too. They just stuck us in a conference room for two hours with this guy who flew in from Chicago. He talked so fast and used all this jargon, and I just kept looking at his tie. It was this really loud geometric pattern, like something from the eighties. It reminded me of a tie my dad used to wear to church when I was a kid. He had this whole collection of novelty ties. One of them played "Jingle Bells" if you pressed a little button hidden in the back. My brother and I used to sneak into his closet and press it just to annoy our mom. She hated that tie. She was always trying to "accidentally" lose it at the dry cleaners, but my dad was onto her. He actually started hand-washing it in the bathroom sink. Which is ridiculous, really, because you're not supposed to submerge anything with a battery pack in it, right? I'm pretty sure he shorted it out eventually, because it stopped playing the music. But he still wore it every Christmas Eve...

Um, anyway, sorry. What was the question? Stress? Yeah, I don't really know if being upset or stressed changes my focus. It just feels like my brain is always kind of slippery, no matter how I'm feeling.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: What finally pushed me to come in is that I can start an EPIC quality report or sit down in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking it, and within a few minutes my mind has drifted so far that I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the whole point of the discussion.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S002).

patient.answer:
Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um... well, what finally pushed me to come in is that I'm just really struggling at work lately. I manage a health clinic, so I do a lot of data tracking, and I can start pulling an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in one of our clinic metrics meetings with every intention of paying attention. Actually, we just had a huge meeting on Tuesday because the new compliance guidelines came down from corporate, and they want everything color-coded on the new dashboards now, which honestly feels a bit redundant since the old system worked perfectly fine for the last five years. They used to have this terrible salad bar where the cucumbers were always slimy, but now they have a hot food station. I had their meatloaf on Tuesday, and it wasn't half bad. It reminded me of the meatloaf my grandmother used to make. She always put a hard-boiled egg right in the middle of it. Have you ever seen that? When you slice it, there's a perfect circle of egg in every piece. She used to serve it with these mashed potatoes that had way too much butter in them, but they were so good. She had this beautiful vintage potato ricer that made them perfectly smooth... 

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely lost the thread. I'm sorry. You were asking about distractions versus attention. Honestly, I really don't know if it's my surroundings pulling me away or just my own brain wandering off on its own. I haven't really noticed a pattern, just that my mind won't stay where I need it to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily related to attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or another condition
doctor.question: Do you think your difficulty with focus is something that you experience across all situations, or are there specific times or activities where you feel more focused and able to concentrate?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a follow-up question about situational focus or hyperfocus, which does not directly map to any of the remaining unaddressed symptom profiles such as listening difficulty, instruction follow-through, avoidance of mental effort, losing items, onset, or duration.

patient.answer:
I'm really not sure. I haven't noticed any specific times where I feel more focused, honestly. I've actually tried to find things that might hold my attention better, just to see. Like, a few months ago I decided to take up knitting, thinking maybe keeping my hands busy would help me zone in. 

I went down to this lovely little yarn shop on Main Street, the one right next to the old art deco movie theater. The owner there, her name is Barbara, she was incredibly helpful. She has this beautiful golden retriever that just sleeps in the corner of the shop all day. He is the sweetest thing, his name is Barnaby. I used to have a golden retriever when I was in my twenties. They really are just the absolute best dogs, so gentle and loyal. Mine used to love swimming in the lake behind our first house. We had this old wooden dock out back that was always giving everyone splinters. My husband at the time tried to sand it down one summer, but the wood was just too rotted. We eventually had to replace the whole thing with that composite decking material, which is so much more expensive up front, but honestly it's worth it because you never have to stain it. Staining a deck is such backbreaking work, especially in the humidity we get around here in July... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, if I can concentrate better on certain things. No, I don't think so. Because even with the knitting, I just end up dropping stitches or losing count of my rows because my mind wanders off to something else entirely. So yeah, I can't really think of any situation where the focus comes easily.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's difficulty with focus is related to emotional distress
doctor.question: Do you feel like your difficulty with focus is worse when you're stressed or upset about something?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the difficulty focusing is exacerbated by stress or emotional distress, which is not covered by any of the specific symptom profiles provided.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't really know if stress makes it worse. I haven't really paid attention to that. I guess I'm always a little stressed? Working at the clinic is just constant pressure. Especially with the new electronic health record system they rolled out last quarter. It was supposed to streamline everything, but the interface is just so clunky. 

The training they gave us for it was completely inadequate, too. They just stuck us in a conference room for two hours with this guy who flew in from Chicago. He talked so fast and used all this jargon, and I just kept looking at his tie. It was this really loud geometric pattern, like something from the eighties. It reminded me of a tie my dad used to wear to church when I was a kid. He had this whole collection of novelty ties. One of them played "Jingle Bells" if you pressed a little button hidden in the back. My brother and I used to sneak into his closet and press it just to annoy our mom. She hated that tie. She was always trying to "accidentally" lose it at the dry cleaners, but my dad was onto her. He actually started hand-washing it in the bathroom sink. Which is ridiculous, really, because you're not supposed to submerge anything with a battery pack in it, right? I'm pretty sure he shorted it out eventually, because it stopped playing the music. But he still wore it every Christmas Eve...

Um, anyway, sorry. What was the question? Stress? Yeah, I don't really know if being upset or stressed changes my focus. It just feels like my brain is always kind of slippery, no matter how I'm feeling.
